newsitem.title: POLAND: EBRD mulls 25 pct of Polish shipyard for $100 mln.
newsitem.headline: EBRD mulls 25 pct of Polish shipyard for $100 mln.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is in negotiations on buying up to 25 percent of Poland's biggest Szczecin shipyard for some $100 million, an industry official said on Friday.
Ryszard Ferworn, president of the Centromor trading company in which the shipyard has a 22.5-percent stake, told Reuters the deal could be concluded by early March.
EBRD spokeswoman said the bank was in discussions with Szczecin, but could not confirm any figures or dates. Szczecin officials were not immediately available for comment.

In the Szczecin shipyard employees now have 34.7 percent of shares, a group of four Polish banks have 30 percent, with 15 percent in the hands of Capital Group Ltd, nine percent owned by the management and 5.3 percent among small shareholders.
Six percent is in the hands of the state treasury.
It was not clear if the potential EBRD deal would entail a new issue or buying existing shares.
Ferworn said the shipyard would use the cash to set up a holding and buy stakes in the Gdynia shipyard and ship-engine maker H. Cegielski from the city of Poznan.
Ferworn's Centromor would become a part of the holding, he said.

Janusz Sniadek, head of the Gdynia shipyard supervisory board, told Reuters the capital ties within such a holding were currently being examined by a commission of the shipyard's shareholders and employees.
"The project envisages that the Szczecin shipyard will take over 51.8 percent of the Gdynia yard," Sniadek said.
He said Szczecin would first buy 18 percent of Gdynia's existing shares and then raise Gdynia's current share capital of 125 million zlotys by 98 million zlotys by buying a new share issue.

After the deal Gdynia's shareholders would include Szczecin with a 51.8 percent stake, the state treasury with a 17.38 percent stake, state-owned commercial Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA with 12.4 percent and Bank Handlowy SA with 11.3 percent. The rest would belong to small shareholders.
The Szczecin shipyard would also buy a 50 percent stake of the H. Cegielski ship-engine plant for 70.2 million zlotys.
